root_cause.text: The bounds check in `check_xattrs()` for the next xattr entry pointer `next` only verified `next < end`, without ensuring there was enough space for the subsequent 4-byte read by `IS_LAST_ENTRY()`, allowing an out-of-bounds read when `next` points near the end of the valid region.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description and commit message state: "The bounds check for the next xattr entry in check_xattrs() uses (void *)next >= end, which allows next to point within sizeof(u32) bytes of end. On the next loop iteration, IS_LAST_ENTRY() reads 4 bytes via *(__u32 *)(entry), which can overrun the valid xattr region." The patch changes the condition to `(void *)next + sizeof(u32) > end` to fix this.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix a potential out-of-bounds access in check_xattrs by adding a size guard for the next attribute entry.
intent_record.what: Changed the condition in the loop inside check_xattrs() from checking if (void *)next >= end to checking if (void *)next + sizeof(u32) > end.
intent_record.how: The change ensures that when iterating over extended attribute entries, there is enough remaining buffer space to read at least the first 4 bytes (probably the entry size) of the next entry, preventing a potential out-of-bounds read past the buffer end.
